title: Wren and the Ledger
premise: In the port city of Vellamare, on the eve of revolution, Wendell 'Wren' Halloran has spent her life passing as a boy in her father's print shop, cutting type and keeping the ledger of debts owed by powerful men. When a stranger named Ivo arrives clutching pages written in the hand of Aldous Renner — the reformist printer officially executed two years ago — Wren realizes her father's ledger holds proof of who betrayed him, and that her own family is implicated. As the city ignites, an evacuation ship offers one last berth, forcing Wren to choose between saving her father, whose corruption she can no longer deny, or Ivo, who carries the truth that could remake the nation. In the end, Wren gives up the berth herself, stays behind to print the evidence as the mob closes in, and escapes through the print shop's cellar tunnels — alive, unmasked, and finally the author of her own name.
about_author: Sable Crane is the pen name of a former letterpress apprentice turned archivist who spent a decade cataloguing underground pamphlets from failed revolutions. Wren and the Ledger is their first novel, drawn from marginalia found in seized printing ledgers.

chapters.title: The Weight of Sorts
chapters.summary: POV: Wren. In the Halloran print shop, Wren cuts type by lamplight while measuring what can be carried in a satchel — a habit born of her mother's flight years ago. Her father Wendell Sr. burns a bundle of correspondence and warns her to forget it. Emotional beat: quiet dread beneath routine; the reader learns Wren's secret identity and her father's first lie.

chapters.title: A Stranger's Hand
chapters.summary: POV: Wren. Ivo Marchetti arrives at closing time with three pages of unmistakable handwriting — Aldous Renner's, the martyr executed two years past. He claims Renner lives and needs the ledger of debts the shop keeps for the Governor's Council. Wren's father denies everything too quickly. Emotional beat: fascination curdling into suspicion; Wren recognizes the handwriting because she once forged it.

chapters.title: What the Ledger Owes
chapters.summary: POV: Wren. Alone at night, Wren deciphers the ledger's coded columns and finds payments from the Council to an informant — initials matching her father — dated the week of Renner's supposed execution. She confronts nothing, but copies the page. Emotional beat: the loyalty-versus-truth theme crystallizes; grief arrives before certainty.

chapters.title: The Council's Courtesy
chapters.summary: POV: alternating Wren and Ivo. A courteous visit from Council secretary Madame Voss makes clear the family is being watched. Ivo reveals he was Renner's apprentice and that the 'corpse' was another man entirely. Wren must decide whether to tell him about the informant's initials. Emotional beat: two liars circling each other, each needing the other.

chapters.title: Riots in the Ink Quarter
chapters.summary: POV: Ivo. Bread riots ignite the printing district; presses are smashed as tools of propaganda. Ivo saves Wren from a mob that mistakes her for a Council clerk, and in the aftermath she shows him the copied ledger page. His face when he reads his father-figure's betrayal is the chapter's wound. Emotional beat: alliance sealed in shared disillusionment.

chapters.title: Renner, Alive and Lesser
chapters.summary: POV: Wren. In a smugglers' warehouse they meet Aldous Renner himself — gaunt, paranoid, less a prophet than a man hoarding grievances. He wants the ledger not for justice but leverage over the Council. Wren sees power already corrupting the revolution's saint. Emotional beat: disenchantment deepening; the truth is no longer clean.

chapters.title: One Berth
chapters.summary: POV: alternating. The harbor master, bribed by Ivo, secures passage on the last ship out before the naval blockade — one berth only. Voss offers Wren's father immunity in exchange for the ledger and the girl who copied it. Wendell Sr. agrees. Emotional beat: the choice sharpens from abstract to unbearable; time begins running out in hours.

chapters.title: The Father's Confession
chapters.summary: POV: Wren. Confronted, her father confesses he informed on Renner to protect the shop — and Wren's secret — after Voss discovered a sample of her forged hand. His betrayal and his love are the same act. He begs her to take the berth. Emotional beat: the novel's moral center; forgiveness offered without absolution.

chapters.title: Print It Before Dawn
chapters.summary: POV: Ivo. Climax. Rather than flee, Wren and Ivo set the type themselves and run off five hundred copies of the ledger on the old press while Voss's men batter the door. Renner arrives demanding the original for himself; when refused, he betrays their location. Emotional beat: fury and purpose fused — the press becomes the weapon.

chapters.title: The Last Impression
chapters.summary: POV: Wren. Resolution. The pamphlets flood the streets as the ship sails without them; her father takes the berth at Wren's insistence, weeping. Guided by the smugglers' cellar tunnels, Wren escapes the burning quarter carrying only her type case and her true name spoken aloud for the first time. Epilogue beat: months later, a new press prints under the imprint 'Halloran & Marchetti' — identity claimed, truth survived.
